page: OVHcloud b3-128 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores with 32 vCPUs, operating without hyperthreading at one thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and Passmark CPU scores, alongside high memory read and write bandwidths. It demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, processing 74.67 million Redis SET operations per second, and shows strong performance in software compilation and ray tracing. However, single-threaded performance, such as single-core Geekbench scores and gzip compression, falls within the average range.

The lack of hyperthreading means each vCPU maps to a dedicated physical core, ensuring consistent compute performance without resource sharing at the core level. The 400 GB NVMe SSD provides fast local storage, though it is fixed in size. This profile is suited for multi-threaded workloads, database hosting, software compilation, and moderate-scale text or image processing. It is less optimal for tasks requiring high single-threaded clock speeds or massive local storage arrays.
description: OVHcloud b3-128 is a general-purpose server instance featuring 32 dedicated physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz with x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, a 400 GB local NVMe SSD, and an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, the server allocates one thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading to deliver consistent compute performance. Benchmark results place this instance in the top tier for multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and database operations, including 74.67 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded tasks and static web serving throughput perform in the average range. This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded applications, database hosting, software compilation, and parallel processing workloads.
